title: Gangster Himanshu Bhau Arrested in Las Vegas After Indian Tip-Off
excerpt: Tracked by Delhi and Haryana police teams and shared with US law enforcement, the red-notice fugitive was arrested Thursday evening alongside Neeraj Faridpuria; Indian agencies are now pushing to expedite his deportation.
body:
• US law enforcement arrested fugitive gangster Himanshu Bhau in Las Vegas on Thursday evening after Indian agencies tracked his location and shared the coordinates, an NIA source told the Indian Express.
  • Bhau, from Ritoli village in Haryana's Rohtak district, faces more than 30 cases — at least 16 of them for murder or attempted murder — and has been the subject of an Interpol red notice since August 2023.
  • Another fugitive, Neeraj Faridpuria, was picked up in the same operation; he had allegedly removed an ankle-bracelet tracker after being detained and released on bail in the US this year.
  • Indian agencies are now coordinating with US authorities to expedite deportation, and a team of senior Indian officers is likely to travel to the US to complete the paperwork — the step that decides how soon Bhau faces trial in India.

One of India's most wanted gangsters is in US custody. Himanshu Bhau, who Indian police say ran an extortion and murder syndicate across Delhi, Haryana and Punjab from abroad, was arrested in Las Vegas on Thursday evening after Indian central agencies alerted US law enforcement to his location, according to the Indian Express. Fugitive Neeraj Faridpuria was arrested alongside him.

Tracked to Las Vegas

A source in the National Investigation Agency told the Indian Express that multiple teams of the Delhi Police and Haryana Police had been working to trace Bhau in the United States, where an Interpol red notice has been in force against him since August 2023.

"With the help of technical surveillance and on the basis of source-based information, his location in Las Vegas was tracked down and the coordinates were shared with the LEA (law enforcement agencies) in the US, which made the arrest Thursday evening."

— NIA source, quoted by the Indian Express

Faridpuria's capture closes a second escape route: according to the Indian Express and Dainik Bhaskar's reporting, he had been detained in the US and released on bail this year, then evaded arrest after removing the ankle-bracelet tracker fitted to him. Indian agencies are now coordinating with US authorities to expedite deportation proceedings for both men, the NIA source said, and a special team of senior officers is likely to visit the US to complete the documentation.

A Crime Career That Began at 17

Bhau, in his early twenties and also known as Kunal, is a native of Ritoli village in Rohtak. The Indian Express reports he began with extortion in Rohtak's Subzi Mandi area, allegedly killed a local youth, Sunny of Ritoli village, and escaped from a juvenile correctional facility in Hisar in 2020. After the escape he joined local criminals, including jailed gangster Neeraj Bawana, before forming his own gang. He has over 30 cases against him, at least 16 for murder and attempt to murder, the source said. Dainik Bhaskar reports the case list spans murder, attempted murder, extortion and arms smuggling across several states, with rewards of Rs 2.5 lakh announced by Haryana Police and Rs 1 lakh by Delhi Police. He first drew national attention in 2022, when his name surfaced in three murders within 24 hours in Haryana.

Running a Gang From Abroad

Before a lookout circular could be issued, Bhau obtained a passport from Bareilly in August 2022 using forged papers in the name of Kunal Singh and fled the country, the Indian Express reports. He flew to the United Arab Emirates and then took the irregular "dunki" route to Europe, running his syndicate from Portugal with the help of Yogesh Kadian alias Bobby, his relative Sahil and Faridpuria. The method, investigators say, was remote: threatening calls from abroad, firing outside the homes of businessmen who refused to pay, and recruiting young men through social media. His gang has claimed responsibility for the 2025 firing outside YouTuber Elvish Yadav's home in Gurugram, and his name has figured in cases including a murder at a Burger King outlet in Delhi's Rajouri Garden. Faridpuria works with Punjab's Bambiha gang, a rival of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, with which Bhau is also reported to be in conflict. In a recent coordination meeting, Haryana Police told central agencies the state has around 80 active criminal gangs, naming Bhau's among the majors.

What Happens Next

The arrest itself is the midpoint, not the end. Bhau's return depends on US deportation or extradition proceedings, which Indian agencies say they are working to expedite, with officers expected to travel to complete the paperwork. For the businesses across Delhi-NCR and Haryana that have faced extortion calls in his gang's name, his custody in the US is the first concrete step toward a trial in India — and a test of how quickly the two systems can move a red-notice fugitive from a Las Vegas arrest to an Indian courtroom.
